Zambia Lifts Three-Week Copper Export Ban, Operations Resume at Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd

Zambia’s government has lifted a temporary export ban on copper concentrates and refined copper, bringing relief to the country’s vital metals and mining industry after nearly three weeks of disruption. The measure, which was introduced on May 22 in an effort to address irregularities in export documentation and improve revenue collection, halted outbound shipments from major smelters, including Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd.

The Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development announced on Monday that the ban was rescinded following the implementation of a new digital tracking system for copper cargo and the harmonization of customs procedures at key border crossings. Mines Minister Paul Kabuswe stated, “We are committed to ensuring transparency and accountability in our mineral exports. The temporary suspension allowed us to close loopholes and strengthen oversight without compromising the competitiveness of Zambian copper on global markets.”

Industry sources estimate that the ban delayed the export of more than 45,000 tonnes of copper, valued at over $400 million at current prices. Production at smelters and concentrators was scaled back during the period, with inventories piling up at facilities such as Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd and Northern Minerals Processing.

“The halt put a strain on working capital and created logistical challenges, but we are now back to normal operations,” said an executive at Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd. “We appreciate the government’s engagement with stakeholders to resolve the impasse.”

The Zambian Chamber of Mines welcomed the move, noting that the industry is expected to recover quickly from the supply backlog. “Export flows have resumed and we anticipate that shipments will normalize within the next two weeks as border procedures stabilize,” said spokesperson Grace Mwansa.

Analysts say the resolution of the export ban will help Zambia maintain its position as Africa’s second-largest copper producer and reassure international buyers. “This episode underscores the importance of clear, predictable trade policies for the mining sector, which is central to Zambia’s economy,” said Jacob Banda, an independent industry consultant.

No further export restrictions are currently anticipated, according to official statements. The government has pledged ongoing dialogue with mining companies to ensure compliance with new documentation requirements and to prevent future disruptions.
